## Spec Grounding

A drafted story is grounded in the project's spec, never written from the request alone. Before proposing, the drafter searches the spec for what each story touches: the requirements and behaviours it changes or relies on, the names it uses, as a feature, a component, or a property, and the sections they are in. It reads the spec as every run does, from its compiled reference or from what `piton slice` prints, never from the Piton source, as the [ModeSystemPrompts](../prompt-mode/mode-system-prompts/index.md#mode-system-prompts) says, and the planning prompt of the [BakedSystemPrompts](../harness-integration/baked-prompts/index.md#baked-system-prompts) tells it to.
Each proposal cites what it found, specifically: its `suspense-story` block holds a `spec` list, one entry per element, each a link to the compiled reference heading it comes from, as `.claude/reference/scope/planning/index.md#sprint`, with a short line of what in it the story touches, and the story's prompt names those elements and links to them, as a prompt written for a mode does, so the run it is sent to reads them first. Only elements the drafter found are cited: a link must point at a heading that exists in the compiled reference, and the application checks each one when the proposal arrives, dropping any that doesn't, with a muted note on the card saying which link it dropped and why.
Where no spec element matches part of a story, as a request for something the spec doesn't describe yet, the story says so instead of inventing one: its `spec` list holds an entry reading "No match", with what was looked for, and its prompt says plainly that the spec has nothing on it yet, so the change is new. A proposal with no element at all, and no "No match", isn't shown as a story: its card says the drafter cited no spec, in the theme's warning colour, with "Draft again", which runs the draft for that story once more.
The citations are shown on the proposal's card, beneath its prompt, as a short list, each element's name and section as a link that opens the compiled reference there, a "No match" entry muted with a small marker, and are kept with the story once it is accepted, listed in the open story beneath its steps as "Spec", and shown in its row's tooltip. They can be edited with the story, removed, or added to by hand from the compiled reference.
Each proposal is a card in the panel, in the order given: a label at its top, "New story" in the theme's accent or "Add to" and the story's title in Spec's or the story's own mode's colour; its title, its mode pill, and its prompt beneath, clipped at four lines with "Read more"; and three buttons along its foot, "Accept", "Edit", and "Reject", reachable by Tab and labelled for a screen reader. Edit opens the card's title, prompt, mode, and target in place, the target a menu of "New story" and each story, to be changed before it is accepted; editing doesn't accept it. Reject removes the card, with a short "Undo" in its place for a few seconds.
Accept records it in the plan straight away, saved as any change to the plan is: a new story goes into Next sprint, at its end, in its mode, marked "From agent" with a small sparkle beside its title until it is first opened; an addition is added to the named story as a new step at its end, as its steps say, its attachments with it, and the story is marked "Updated by agent" until it is next opened, the new step shown highlighted the first time it is; where the story no longer exists by then, the step isn't added, as the steps say, and the card stays, its target changed to "New story", to be accepted again. A story already sent can't be added to: its proposals offer only "New story". Each card, once decided, goes from the panel, and an accepted one leaves a one-line muted note in its place, "Added to Next sprint" or "Added to <story>", with a link that opens it.
Ask answers can propose the same way: a `suspense-story` block in an answer is shown as a proposal card, with the same Accept, Edit, and Reject, its accepting recording it in the plan as above, so a story can come out of a conversation without anything written silently.

## Research
## Reading The Spec

In every mode, the harness learns what the spec says from its compiled reference, the Markdown the spec build writes under HARNESS_DIRECTORY's reference folder, where inheritance, expressions, and links are already resolved, or, for one thing, from what `piton slice` prints for it with the adapter of the harness in use. It never reads the Piton source under the spec location to learn what the spec says. To a run that can see the spec location, the system template and the spec-reading prompt say so, and name the spec location only as where edits to the spec go. A question sees the spec location too, read only, so it can run `piton slice` there, and is told the same: that the spec is read from the compiled reference or from what `piton slice` prints, never from the Piton source. A question makes no edits, so the Ask instructions name the spec location for what it is, the spec's Piton source, that `piton slice` reads, which a question never changes, and nothing told to a question says or suggests that it may edit the spec. A run that can't see the spec location is told only that the spec is read from the compiled reference, with nothing about the spec source.

## Writing The Spec

content.text:
Drafted stories now have to cite the project's spec. Tests pass in a scratch copy of the project: the planning, sprint, card and answer-block tests, including new ones for reading and checking citations and for a proposal with none. I haven't tried it in the running app, and the type tidy-up I made after the last test run (pulling the reference-opening callback into a named type) hasn't been rebuilt.

- **The drafting prompt:** `planning.pi` now tells the drafter to search the spec before proposing. It must read the compiled reference or `piton slice`, never the Piton source, cite only headings it actually found, and name and link them in the story's prompt. Where nothing fits, it writes a "No match" entry saying what it looked for, and says in the prompt that the spec has nothing on it yet. The request shows an example `suspense-story` block with a `spec:` list, using the project's own reference folder.
- **Checking links:** Suspense checks every cited link when a proposal arrives. It must be a heading that exists in the compiled reference. Any that isn't is dropped, with a muted note on the card saying which link and why.
- **No citations at all:** a proposal with no citation and no "No match" can't be accepted. Its card shows a warning-coloured "the drafter cited no spec" line and a "Draft again" button, which reruns drafting for just that story.
- **On the card:** citations appear under the prompt as clickable links that open the reference page. "No match" entries are muted, with a small marker.
- **After accepting:**
  - Citations are kept with the story in `order.json`, and an accepted addition merges its citations into the story's.
  - The open story lists them as "Spec" beneath its steps, each removable, with a box to add one by hand. The same link check applies there.
  - The row shows a small book icon whose tooltip lists them.

**Gaps against the spec:**
- **Opening a link:** it opens the reference page but doesn't jump to the heading.
- **Editing an entry:** a citation can only be edited by removing it and adding it again.
- **Ask answers:** story cards in Ask answers don't show their citations yet. Their citations are still checked and kept when accepted.
